# Flagcn: complete reference for AI agents

Flagcn is a shadcn registry for accessible React flag components. It copies source files into the user's project through the shadcn CLI. It is not an npm runtime package.

## Canonical machine-readable resources

- Short index: /llms.txt
- Complete reference: /llms-full.txt
- Agent instructions: /AGENTS.md
- Registry index: /r/registry.json
- Registry item pattern: /r/{name}.json
- Human documentation: /docs
- Complete visual catalog: /flags

Resolve relative paths against the origin from which this file was fetched.

## Inventory

- 306 flag entries.
- Countries, territories, organizations, and selected subdivisions.
- Universal primitive: @flagcn/flag.
- Searchable picker: @flagcn/flag-picker.
- Country foundation: @flagcn/country-data and @flagcn/calling-codes.
- Country controls: @flagcn/country-picker, @flagcn/country-select, @flagcn/country-badge, @flagcn/flag-avatar.
- International phone input: @flagcn/phone-input.
- Locale controls: @flagcn/language-picker, @flagcn/currency-picker, @flagcn/currency.
- Regional collections: @flagcn/gcc and @flagcn/eu-collection.
- Typed wrappers: @flagcn/{lowercase-code}, for example @flagcn/ae and @flagcn/us-ca.
- Complete install: @flagcn/all.
- Formats: svg, png, webp, jpg.
- Ratios: 4x3, 1x1, original.
- Default format: svg.
- Default ratio: 4x3.
- Source license: MIT.
- SVG artwork: Flag Icons 7.5.0 for supported 4:3 and 1:1 assets.
- Raster artwork and SVG fallbacks: FlagCDN, sourced by Flagpedia.

## Connect the registry

`@flagcn` is listed in the official shadcn Registry Directory. Current shadcn CLI releases resolve it directly, without a project-local registry entry.

If an older CLI snapshot does not recognize the namespace, use this compatibility fallback. Replace FLAGCN_ORIGIN with the origin that served this document.

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@flagcn": {
      "url": "FLAGCN_ORIGIN/r/{name}.json"
    }
  }
}
```

After directory acceptance, the same namespaced commands can work without project-local configuration.

## Install commands

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/flag
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/flag-picker
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/country-picker
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/phone-input
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/language-picker
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/currency-picker
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/ae
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/all
```

Package manager equivalents for @flagcn/ae:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/ae
yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @flagcn/ae
bunx --bun shadcn@latest add @flagcn/ae
```

Use one named item when the interface needs a fixed flag. Use @flagcn/flag for dynamic codes, @flagcn/country-picker for country selection, and the focused phone/language/currency items for locale forms. Use @flagcn/all only when the complete typed catalog is genuinely needed.

## Search and discovery

Inspect registry metadata before installing an item:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest view @flagcn/ae
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest search @flagcn -q "United Arab Emirates"
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest list @flagcn
```

`view` shows an item and its dependencies, `search` matches registry names and descriptions, and `list` returns the complete Flagcn catalog. These commands do not install files.

## Universal Flag component

Typical import after installation:

```tsx
import { Flag } from "@/components/flags/flag"

export function Market() {
  return (
    <Flag
      code="ae"
      format="svg"
      ratio="4x3"
      width={80}
      alt="United Arab Emirates flag"
      className="rounded-sm"
    />
  )
}
```

### Flag props

- code: string, required. Lowercase ISO-style code such as ae, jp, gb-eng, or us-ca. Runtime input is trimmed and lowercased.
- alt: string. Defaults to an uppercase-code description, but context-specific text is recommended.
- format: "svg" | "png" | "webp" | "jpg". Default: "svg".
- width: positive number. Default: 80. Used for rendered width and CDN source selection.
- ratio: "4x3" | "1x1" | "original". Default: "4x3".
- decorative: boolean. Default: false. When true, emits alt="" and aria-hidden.
- sizes: forwarded; a width-matching value is generated for raster srcSet when omitted.
- loading: forwarded. Default: "lazy".
- decoding: forwarded. Default: "async".
- className, style, ref, id, title, events, fetchPriority, crossOrigin, data attributes, and other standard React img props are forwarded.
- src and srcSet cannot be overridden because the component owns source construction.

The component renders a native img and no wrapper element.

## Formats and ratios

SVG uses pinned Flag Icons sources for supported 4:3 and 1:1 assets. U.S. state SVGs and original-proportion SVGs use FlagCDN as a fallback. PNG, WebP, and JPEG receive responsive srcSet candidates. Pass a custom sizes value when the visual width changes with media queries.

The 4x3 ratio provides consistent landscape tiles and is the default. The 1x1 ratio creates a square image box. Both fixed frames use object-fit: contain so the complete flag remains visible. The original ratio preserves the source artwork's proportions.

Recommended combinations:

- General UI: svg + 4x3.
- Dense square picker treatment without clipping: webp + 1x1.
- Accurate editorial display: svg + original.
- Raster-only downstream workflow: webp, png, or jpg when JPEG is required.

## URL utilities

The flag registry item includes typed helpers:

- getFlagUrl(code, { format, width, ratio }): returns one pinned Flag Icons or FlagCDN URL.
- getFlagSrcSet(code, { format, width, ratio }): returns undefined for SVG and a width descriptor list for PNG/WebP/JPEG.
- normalizeFlagCode(code): trims, lowercases, and validates supported ISO-style syntax.
- flagFormats: readonly ["svg", "png", "webp", "jpg"].
- flagRatios: readonly ["4x3", "1x1", "original"].

## FlagPicker

```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { FlagPicker } from "@/components/flags/flag-picker"
import type { FlagCode } from "@/components/flags/flag-data"

export function CountryField() {
  const [country, setCountry] = React.useState<FlagCode>("ae")
  return <FlagPicker value={country} onValueChange={setCountry} kinds={["country"]} name="country" aria-label="Market" />
}
```

Important props:

- value: controlled FlagCode.
- defaultValue: initial uncontrolled FlagCode.
- onValueChange: callback receiving a FlagCode.
- format: svg | png | webp | jpg. Default: svg.
- ratio: 4x3 | 1x1 | original. Default: 4x3.
- kinds: array of country, subdivision, or organization.
- codes: explicit FlagCode array used to constrain results.
- disabledCodes: visible but unavailable FlagCode array.
- showCode and showCallingCode: control trailing metadata.
- placeholder: trigger/search placeholder.
- aria-label: accessible name for the combobox trigger. Defaults to the placeholder and selected flag name.
- name: adds a hidden form input carrying the selected code.
- disabled and className are supported.

The picker is searchable and keyboard operable. Country records match English/native names, aliases, ISO-2, ISO-3, and calling codes. It uses the consuming project's shadcn Tabler icon convention.

## Country data and utilities

`@flagcn/country-data` installs generated typed country records and helpers. Records include lowercase code, ISO alpha-2/alpha-3/numeric values, English and native names, aliases, emoji, calling codes, continent, capital, currencies, and languages.

Important helpers:

- `getCountry(code)` and `getCountryByAlpha3(alpha3)`.
- `searchCountries(query)` across names, aliases, codes, capitals, calling codes, currencies, and languages.
- `countryCodeToEmoji(code)` and `emojiToCountryCode(emoji)`.
- `getCountryCallingCodes(code)`.
- `getCountriesByCallingCode(code)`, which intentionally returns an array because calling codes can be shared.

The data is generated from `countries-list`, `i18n-iso-countries`, and `libphonenumber-js`; the generated source is copied into the consumer project. Generation validates unique ISO identifiers, emoji round-trips, language and currency references, and phone calling codes. `countryDataMeta` exposes the pinned source versions and validation state. `phoneCountryCodes` is the narrower set supported by libphonenumber metadata.

## Country components

- `CountryPicker`: country-only FlagPicker with typed CountryCode values and optional country constraints.
- `CountrySelect`: native shadcn select with emoji and optional calling-code labels.
- `CountryBadge`: shadcn Badge plus a flag and name, ISO code, calling code, or no label.
- `FlagAvatar`: shadcn Avatar with a 1:1 flag source and typed fallback.
- `gccCountryCodes` / `isGccCountry`: six current GCC members.
- `euCountryCodes` / `isEuCountry`: 27 current EU members.

## PhoneInput

`@flagcn/phone-input` composes CountryPicker with the consumer project's shadcn Input tokens and declares `libphonenumber-js`. It renders one integrated control with a compact flag/calling-code trigger, supports `sm`, `default`, and `lg` sizes, formats as the user types, normalizes an international `00` prefix, and infers the flag from international or controlled E.164 values. `onValueChange(value, meta)` returns E.164 as `value` when parseable, plus `country`, `formatted`, optional `e164`, `nationalNumber`, `countryCallingCode`, `international`, `possible`, and `valid` metadata. Use `phoneCountryCodes` or `countries` to constrain available country codes.

Give `PhoneInput` a visible label with `id`/`htmlFor` or an `aria-label`. Associate help text with `aria-describedby`; when `aria-invalid` is true, point `aria-errormessage` at the rendered error element's `id`.

## Language and currency

`LanguagePicker` searches English/native language names and exposes RTL metadata. Do not use a country flag as the only language label.

`CurrencyPicker` searches ISO code, English/native name, and symbols. `Currency` renders a typed code/name/symbol label. `CurrencyValue` delegates locale-aware amount formatting to `Intl.NumberFormat`.

## Named wrappers

```tsx
import { UnitedArabEmiratesFlag } from "@/components/flags/countries/ae"

<UnitedArabEmiratesFlag width={32} alt="Available in the UAE" />
```

A named wrapper fixes the code prop and forwards the rest of FlagProps. Use /r/registry.json to discover exact item names. The @flagcn/all item installs the primitive, picker, data, aggregate exports, and all 306 named wrapper files.

## Accessibility rules

- Write alt text for the meaning in context, not the visible stripe pattern.
- If adjacent text already communicates the country or market, set decorative.
- Never use a flag as the sole indicator of language, nationality, residency, or state.
- Pair flags with precise visible text; flags and languages do not map one-to-one.
- Treat politically sensitive and official symbols carefully.

## Styling recipes

```tsx
// Visible label provides the accessible name.
<span className="inline-flex items-center gap-2">
  <Flag code="am" width={24} decorative className="rounded-sm ring-1 ring-border" />
  Armenia
</span>

// Square market tile that preserves the full flag.
<Flag code="jp" ratio="1x1" alt="Japan flag" className="size-10 ring-1 ring-border" />

// Responsive raster image.
<Flag code="br" format="webp" width={160} sizes="(max-width: 640px) 80px, 160px" alt="Brazil flag" />
```

## Website catalog and documentation behavior

The public homepage, flag-catalog shell, and documentation content render without a page-level loading state. The gallery module and native flag images load progressively; `Flag` defaults to `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"` unless a caller overrides those native image props.

Each visual-catalog card keeps the install-command copy action in the top corner of the preview. Its footer groups the JSX and selected-image copy actions at the start, keeps download visually separate at the end, and explains every icon or compact action with a tooltip. Real one-pixel card boundaries use a stronger semantic token than the internal stage and footer dividers, so action rows remain visibly attached to the card above them. Every outer edge is card-owned, including the first card in each responsive row across one-, two-, three-, and four-column layouts. The preview and hero grids are centered, evenly cropped, and intentionally light. Every flag sits on an opaque semantic muted frame, so unused image space never reveals the decorative grid. Flag previews remain still on hover. Downloads fetch the remote asset as a blob and save it with a format-appropriate filename instead of navigating the browser to the CDN URL.

Interactive documentation examples expose their exact source through `View Code`. PhoneInput documentation demonstrates genuinely distinct `sm`, `default`, and `lg` controls; preset national display, international display, validation, read-only, and disabled behavior are presented as full-width individual rows. Navigation to a different route resets scroll to the top, while explicit hash links retain anchor behavior.

The persistent header includes an accessible site command menu on desktop and mobile. Open it with the search button or `Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K`, then search flags, components, documentation, or the GitHub repository. Mobile navigation uses a labeled modal sheet, and copy failures are announced both inline and through a toast notification.

## Registry response behavior

- /r/registry.json lists every item.
- /r/flag.json is the universal primitive payload.
- /r/flag-picker.json is the picker payload.
- /r/country-data.json is the typed country foundation.
- /r/phone-input.json is the international phone input.
- /r/language-picker.json and /r/currency-picker.json are locale controls.
- /r/ae.json is an example named wrapper payload.
- /r/all.json is the complete catalog payload.
- Registry responses allow cross-origin GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS.
- Registry routes should return JSON and a real JSON 404 for unknown items.

## Agent workflow

1. Read /llms.txt and this complete reference.
2. Inspect /r/registry.json for exact item names.
3. Inspect /r/{name}.json if exact installed files or dependencies matter.
4. Preserve the consumer project's components.json aliases and shadcn style.
5. Use the official @flagcn namespace directly; configure its URL only as an older-CLI compatibility fallback.
6. Run the appropriate shadcn CLI command.
7. Import the copied source through the project's existing alias.
8. Supply meaningful alt text or explicitly set decorative.
9. Run the consumer project's typecheck, lint, and tests.

## Licensing and third-party rights

Flagcn original source code is MIT licensed. The repository includes LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Flag Icons is MIT licensed. Flagcn requests version 7.5.0 SVG assets at runtime for supported 4:3 and 1:1 flags. The required copyright and permission notice is preserved in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Flagpedia states that its flag images are public domain and free for commercial and non-commercial use, with attribution appreciated but not required. Raster artwork, U.S. state SVGs, and original-proportion SVGs are delivered from https://flagcdn.com and documented at https://flagpedia.net/about.

Public-domain status does not override laws or protocols governing use of national flags, seals, emblems, or other official symbols. Users remain responsible for accurate use in their jurisdictions and markets.

## Project constraints and truthfulness

- Flagcn depends on remote jsDelivr and FlagCDN availability unless the installed source is modified to self-host artwork.
- The name @flagcn is included in the official shadcn Registry Directory and works without a project-local registry entry in current CLI releases.
- The deployed origin must replace any development or example origin in generated registry payloads.
- Display names are human labels; registry item codes are the stable identifiers.
